paragraphs: Word got around fast — before long, the leaders and friends back in Jerusalem had heard the news: the non-Jewish "outsiders" were now "in." When Peter got back to Jerusalem, some of his old friends — the ones big on circumcision — confronted him: "What do you think you're doing, hanging out with those people? Eating food we're not supposed to eat and wrecking our reputation?"

So Peter started from the very beginning and walked them through it, step by step: "Not long ago I was in Joppa, praying. I fell into a trance and saw a vision: something like a huge blanket, let down by ropes tied to its four corners, came down out of heaven and landed on the ground right in front of me. Crawling around on that blanket were farm animals, wild animals, reptiles, birds — you name it. I was mesmerized. I took it all in."

"Then I heard a voice: 'Go for it, Peter — kill and eat.' I said, 'No way, Master. I've never in my life tasted food that wasn't kosher.' The voice came back: 'If God says it's okay, it's okay.' This happened three times — and then the blanket was pulled back up into the sky."

"Right then, three men showed up at the house where I was staying — sent from Caesarea to get me. The Spirit told me to go with them, no questions asked. So I went — me and six friends — to the man who'd sent for me. He told us how he'd seen an angel right there in his own house, as real as the neighbor next door, saying, 'Send to Joppa for Simon, the one they call Peter. He'll tell you something that will save your life — you and everyone you love.'"

"So I started talking. I hadn't even gotten six sentences out before the Holy Spirit fell on them — exactly like he did on us at the very beginning. That's when I remembered what Jesus said: 'John baptized with water; you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.' So tell me: if God gave them the exact same gift he gave us when we believed in the Master Jesus Christ — who was I to argue with God?"

When they heard the whole story laid out like that, they calmed down. And as it sank in, they started praising God. "It's really happening! God has broken through to the other nations — he's opened up Life to them too!"

Meanwhile, the believers who'd been scattered by the persecution after Stephen's death had traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch — but they were still only telling their fellow Jews. Then some men from Cyprus and Cyrene who'd come to Antioch started talking to Greeks too, giving them the message about the Master Jesus. God was pleased with what they were doing and put his stamp of approval on it — a whole lot of Greeks believed and turned to the Master.

When the church in Jerusalem heard about this, they sent Barnabas to Antioch to check things out. The moment he arrived, he could see God was all over it — behind it and in it. He jumped right in with them, cheering them on, urging them to stick with it for life. That was Barnabas — a good man, full of enthusiasm and confidence in how the Holy Spirit works. The community grew big and strong in the Master.

Then Barnabas headed to Tarsus to look for Saul. He found him and brought him back to Antioch. They stayed there a full year, meeting with the church and teaching tons of people. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.

Around that same time, some prophets came down to Antioch from Jerusalem. One of them, named Agabus, stood up one day and — prompted by the Spirit — warned that a brutal famine was about to hit the whole country. (It did eventually come, during the reign of Claudius.) So the disciples decided each of them would send whatever they could to help their fellow Christians in Judea. They sent Barnabas and Saul to deliver the collection to the leaders in Jerusalem.
title: Peter Explains Himself in Jerusalem
